welcome.script:
Hi, scientists! Welcome to the Field Station, deep in the Florida Everglades.

[ON SCREEN: The hawk]
Meet our hawk. Every morning it sits by boardwalk post 7.

[ON SCREEN: The pellet · Inside the pellet]
Under its branch, Dr. Reyes found this: a pellet. That’s a lump of fur and tiny bones the hawk coughed up. Ew! But it tells us what the hawk ate: mice, frogs, bugs. Never a plant.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
So here’s our case: where did the hawk’s energy really start?

[ON SCREEN: Your clue bar]
Every game you finish adds a clue. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · trace your lunch (Clue 1)

parts.label: 👣 One step back
parts.title: Ask: where did this come from?
rows: Answer each question to take one step back.
Trace at least 2 foods, then list where they started.

warmup.script:
(Hold up a snack, like a cracker or an apple.) I’m about to eat this. But where did its energy come from?

[ON SCREEN: Pick a food]
Pick one of these foods.

[ON SCREEN: One step back]
Now take it back one step at a time. Where did it come from? And what gave THAT its energy? Each right answer adds a step to your trail. Keep going until you can’t go back any further.

Trace two foods, then list where each trail ended. Press Listen. Dr. Reyes has a field tip.

part2.label: Part 2 · the light test (Clue 2) + the marsh photo (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🧪 The light test
parts.title: Change only the light
rows: Pick the light for each tray.

part2.script:
(Cup your hands around a leaf or a plant.) Plants don’t eat. So how do they get food? They make it!

[ON SCREEN: The light test]
Let’s test it. Two trays, same seeds, same soil, same water. You change only the light.

[ON SCREEN: Sunny tray · Dark tray]
Here’s a peek: one grew in a sunny window, one in a dark closet. Hmm, look at that color! Grow both, and check how much food each one made.

[ON SCREEN: The marsh photo]
Then open every number on this real Everglades marsh.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

explore.label: Part 4 · build the hawk’s food chain (Clue 4)

parts.label: ➡ The arrows
parts.title: Explain every arrow
parts.body: Each arrow shows which way the energy moves. The meter fills as your model gets stronger.

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: The grasshopper · The frog]
Meet two more members of the marsh: a grasshopper and a green tree frog.

(Line up three objects on your desk, then point from one to the next.) A food chain is like a line of passes in a game. The energy gets passed along.

[ON SCREEN: Five boxes]
Drag each card into its box. Start where the energy starts! Two cards don’t belong.

[ON SCREEN: The arrows]
Then explain every arrow and watch the meter fill.

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie first.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Where did the hawk’s energy start?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Four places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

parts.label: 🛟 Help buttons
parts.title: Help under every box
rows: Chips light up as you write.
Three hints, one at a time.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You found all four clues! At the top of this tab, crack the case: where did the hawk’s energy really start?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, your own Florida food chain, and a CER.

[ON SCREEN: Help buttons]
Watch the chips light up as you write. Stuck? Press Hint. Your answers save as you type.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The quote
parts.title: Some people say…
parts.body: “Plants don’t really need sunlight. They get their food from the soil.”

parts.label: ⚖ CER
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Claim: what you think is true.
Evidence: facts from the lesson that prove it.
Reasoning: how the facts prove your claim.

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Tap to plan
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.
They drop into your C and E boxes. You write the R.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The quote]
Some people say, “Plants don’t need sunlight. They get their food from the soil.” Hmm. Remember the dark tray?

[ON SCREEN: CER]
Remember CER: your claim, your evidence from today, and your reasoning.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side, then two pieces of evidence. They drop right into your boxes. The reasoning is all you. Try starting with “This shows that…”

Press Listen. Dr. Reyes wants to hear your side.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🍃 Your specimen
parts.title: Sunlit leaf
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: What if a link goes missing?
parts.body: The same marsh, one piece gone.

closing.script:
Case closed! The hawk never ate a plant, but it still runs on sunlight. And so do you!

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and a sunlit leaf goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time, we’ll ask: what happens to the hawk if something in the chain goes missing?

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

part1.label: Part 1 · the Sun is the start
part1.script: (Flip on a flashlight.) A flashlight needs a battery. Almost all life on Earth runs on one giant battery: the Sun. Read Part 1 to find out why animals can’t make their own food.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

partc.label: Part C · your own food chain
partc.script:
[ON SCREEN: Your place]
Now it’s your turn. Pick a Florida place you know. Name one producer and two consumers, then show how the energy moves. Want to draw it? The sketch pad is a bonus.
